entry.content:
fix(review): guest-mode due count and queue waited on a vocabulary map that had not loaded

In demo / guest mode the review summary and the queue were computed from a
ref read once at mount, before the vocabulary finished loading from
localStorage. Guests with words due therefore saw "All caught up!" and an
empty queue. The e2e suite has been catching this (it only runs on
workflow_dispatch), and it is the "Review looks like a stub" symptom for
anyone on the Try Demo path.

- Derive the local summary from the reactive schedule memo, which now also
  counts what is due, and hold the queue load until the map is in. For
  signed-in users the gate is a constant and the Firestore path is unchanged.
- Keep "All caught up!" as the start-button label in the no-words case; the
  card above already explains it, and the e2e contract expects that text.
- Add a `card-front` test id to the review card so the flip-cycle e2e can
  find it, and let the completion e2e accept the "Explicit feliciter"
  colophon that replaced the old "session complete" wording.

Locally: srs-review, mobile-reader e2e green; unit, lint, type-check, build green.

fix(auth): native sign-in errors from TestFlight build 59

entry.title: fix(auth): native sign-in errors from TestFlight build 59
entry.content:
fix(auth): native sign-in errors from TestFlight build 59

Two failures reported from build 59 on an iPhone:

1. "auth.networkError" rendered verbatim after a failed native Google
   sign-in. authService returns i18n keys in AuthResult.error, but the
   social-login handlers in SignIn/SignUp displayed the key as-is and no
   locale defines the auth.* error keys. Pages now render every failure
   through describeAuthError(), which translates known keys with an
   English default, and en.ts gains the missing keys so other locales
   fall back to real prose.

2. "The operation couldn't be completed. (com.apple.AuthenticationServices.
   AuthorizationError error 1001.)" shown as an error after Apple sign-in.
   Error 1001 is ASAuthorizationError.canceled: the user dismissed the
   sheet. @capgo/capacitor-social-login flags this with code
   'USER_CANCELLED' but carries the raw iOS description, which contains
   no "cancel", so the message-only check missed it. isUserCancellation()
   now checks the plugin code and the 1001 value; cancels are silent.

Diagnostics for whatever remains: AuthResult.detail carries the
underlying code + message (including Firebase's customData cause such as
"TypeError: Load failed", and a distinct message when the 25s guard fires),
rendered in small print under the banner and logged to the console, so the
next device screenshot is enough to root-cause a real network failure.

Native Firebase Auth no longer registers browserPopupRedirectResolver:
OAuth on iOS/Android runs through native sheets, never Firebase popups or
redirects, per Firebase's Capacitor guidance.

Tests: authErrors.test.ts pins cancel detection, key-to-prose rendering,
silent Apple cancel, and detail propagation.

entry.title: chore(firestore): drop redundant single-field reviewLogs index
entry.content:
chore(firestore): drop redundant single-field reviewLogs index

Firestore builds single-field indexes automatically, so the composite
entry on reviewLogs(createdAt DESC) is rejected by the Admin API with
"this index is not necessary, configure using single field index
controls", making `firebase deploy --only firestore:indexes` report an
error for that entry. The two-field reviewLogs index
(vocabItemId ASC, createdAt DESC) is valid and stays.

  hidden in production and native builds, so the copy advertised features
  a reviewer cannot find (App Review guideline 2.3, accurate metadata).
- Release notes 1.0.0: same removal, plus a reviewer note explaining why.
- release:check: the iOS GoogleService-Info.plist check is now informational.
  The iOS target does not link the Firebase iOS SDK; native Google Sign-In
  takes VITE_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID, and Xcode Cloud archives validate without
  the file, so it is not a submission gate.
- STORE_SUBMISSION_HANDOFF: document that indexes are not deployed by CI
  and mark the iOS plist optional.

entry.title: fix(auth): honest login page when a provider is unavailable; bump to …
entry.content:
fix(auth): honest login page when a provider is unavailable; bump to build 16

TestFlight build 15 (2026-07-07) predates the native parity audit (b9eb95c)
by 47 commits. This bumps the build number so a current build can be cut, and
fixes the login-page defects that surface when a provider button is hidden.

Login page (SignIn + SignUp):
- The "Or" divider rendered unconditionally while both provider buttons are
  conditional. On Android — where Google needs VITE_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID and
  Apple has no web-flow — the page drew a separator above nothing.
- The Google-linked-account error told users to "sign in with Google above"
  regardless of whether that button exists, leaving a Google-linked user on a
  provider-less build with no route into their account. Now branches on
  showGoogle and points at the web app instead. New "…Web" variants added to
  all 8 locales, alongside the two existing messages that were inline-only.

config:check:native:
- Checked VITE_GOOGLE_IOS_CLIENT_ID but never VITE_GOOGLE_WEB_CLIENT_ID, so
  the Android half of native Google sign-in was invisible to the audit.
- New generic check: warns when .env.native-production is missing values its
  committed .example provides. Xcode Cloud seeds the env file from that
  example (ci_post_clone.sh), so local and cloud builds of the same commit
  could ship different sign-in buttons — exactly the drift found here.

Tests:
- authProviderAvailability.test.ts pins isGoogleSignInAvailable /
  isAppleSignInAvailable across web/iOS/Android × configured/absent. These
  decide which buttons exist and cannot be verified without a device.

Verified: a --mode native-production build now embeds both client ids (it
embedded neither before), and ios-google-scheme.sh injects the reversed-id
URL scheme. Info.plist is deliberately not committed with that scheme — it is
injected at build time.

entry.title: feat(corpus): concurrent AI enrichment driver with quota-safe backoff
entry.content:
feat(corpus): concurrent AI enrichment driver with quota-safe backoff

ai-enrich-served.ts now runs a small worker pool (--concurrency, default 4)
with exponential backoff on 429/503 and a clean stop after persistent
rate-limiting (daily/monthly quota), periodic cache checkpoints every 100
calls, and cache-first application so interrupted runs resume free.

First live batch attempt confirmed the guard works: the user's new
AI Studio key hit its monthly spending cap after the Jonah batch
("RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: monthly spending cap"), and all four runs stopped
cleanly with zero data corruption.
